documents.summary: University AI-guidelines page from the research and innovation office. It says there is no university-wide AI policy, ties AI misuse to the Code of Academic Integrity, requires instructor approval before students use AI, and points instructors to sample syllabus language and department-level guidance.
documents.stance_why: The page states 'there is currently no single, university-wide policy specific to AI' and that 'instructors are encouraged to set clear expectations'; students may use AI only if the instructor approves. The decision is handed to instructors using a Red-Yellow-Green template, so the document stance is delegates.

documents.title: Academic Integrity at the College of Information Science
documents.summary: College of Information Science academic-integrity policy approved by faculty vote in April 2023. It lists generating and submitting AI text or code as prohibited unless an instructor gives written permission, tells students to learn each course's rules, and sets instructor duties and consequences for violations.
documents.stance_why: The policy lists 'Generating and submitting, in whole or in part, text or code through Artificial Intelligence such as ChatGPT' among practices 'PROHIBITED ... unless a given course instructor has specifically written instructions or permission'. AI is banned unless explicitly permitted, so restrict.

units.anchor: adhere to this policy in all academic work including composition of text, computing code
units.fit_note: States scope (text, code, media) rather than defining AI.

units.anchor: Generating and submitting, in whole or in part, text or code through Artificial Intelligence
